t: Ulugh Muhammad occupies Gorodets
c: Ulugh Muhammad continued to exert influence on Moscow, occupying Gorodets in 1444.

t: Ulugh Muhammad attacks Vasily II at Murom
c: Vasily II even wanted him to issue him a patent for the throne, but Ulugh Muhammad attacked him instead at Murom in 1445.

t: Mäxmüd of Kazan founds Khanate of Kazan
c: Unfortunately, Ulugh Muhammad was murdered by his son, Mäxmüd of Kazan, who fled to the middle Volga region and founded the Khanate of Kazan in 1445.

t: Hacı I Giray founds Crimean Khanate
c: In 1449, Hacı I Giray seized Crimea from Ahmad I, and founded the Crimean Khanate.

t: Janibek and Kerei establish Kazakh Khanate
c: After Abu'l-Khayr Khan died in 1467, they assumed leadership over most of his followers, and became the Kazakh Khanate.

t: Küchük Muhammad ousts Sayid Ahmad
c: In 1435, the khan Küchük Muhammad ousted Sayid Ahmad.

t: Sayid Ahmad attacks Moscow
c: Sayid Ahmad continued to raid Muscovy and in 1449 made a direct attack on Moscow.

t: Sayid Ahmad's attack on Moscow fails
c: In 1451, Sayid Ahmad tried to take Moscow again and failed.

t: Golden Horde becomes known as Great Horde
c: Küchük Muhammad was succeeded by his son Mahmud bin Küchük in 1459, from which point on the Golden Horde came to be known as the Great Horde.

t: Ahmed Khan becomes ruler of Great Horde
c: Mahmud was succeeded by his brother Ahmed Khan bin Küchük in 1465.

t: Ahmed kills Abu'l-Khayr Khan
c: In 1469, Ahmed attacked and killed Abu'l-Khayr Khan.

t: Ahmed attacks Moldavia, Poland, Lithuania
c: In the summer of 1470, Ahmed organized an attack against Moldavia, the Kingdom of Poland, and Lithuania.

t: Ahmed demands Ivan III recognize his overlordship
c: In 1474 and 1476, Ahmed insisted that Ivan III, the grand prince of Moscow, recognize the khan as his overlord.

t: Great Stand on the Ugra River
c: In 1480, Ahmed organized a military campaign against Moscow, resulting in a face off between two opposing armies known as the Great Stand on the Ugra River.

t: Crimean Khanate becomes Ottoman vassal state

t: Sheikh Ahmed dies in Kaunas Castle
c: After seeking refuge in Lithuania, Sheikh Ahmed, the last khan of the Great Horde, died in prison in Kaunas Castle some time after 1504.

c: In 1245, Daniel of Galicia's army was dressed in the Mongol fashion after a visit to Batu Khan's camp.

t: Kingdom of Poland conquers Galicia from Mongols
c: Mongol rule in Galicia ended with its conquest by the Kingdom of Poland in 1349.

t: Nizhny Novgorod rebels against Mamai
c: In 1374, Nizhny Novgorod rebelled and slaughtered an embassy sent by Mamai.

c: In 1502, the Horde was absorbed by the Crimean Khanate.

t: Berke allies with Mamluk Sultan Baibars
c: Berke, the Khan of Kipchak had drawn up an alliance with the Mamluk Sultan Baibars against the Ilkhanate in 1261.

t: Berke begins war with Il-Khan Hulagu
c: In 1262, Berke began a war with the Il-Khan Hulagu Khan.

t: Horde siege of Kaffa spreads Black Death
c: In 1347 a Horde siege of the Genoese Crimean port of Kaffa led to the spread of the black death to Europe.

c: In 1502, Meñli I Giray defeated the last khan of the Great Horde, which put an end to the Horde's claims on Crimea.

t: Last major Tatar raid occurs
c: In 1769, a last major Tatar raid resulted in the capture of 20,000 Russian and Ruthenian slaves.

t: İslâm III Giray assists Khmelnytsky Uprising
c: The assistance of İslâm III Giray during the Khmelnytsky Uprising in 1648 contributed greatly to the initial momentum of military successes for the Cossacks.

c: The 1812 Treaty of Bucharest transferred Bessarabia to Russian control.

c: The Duchy of Livonia, tied to Lithuania in real union since the Union of Grodno (1566), became a Polish–Lithuanian condominium.

t: Commonwealth partitioned by powers
c: The Cossack uprisings and foreign interventions led to the partitions of the Commonwealth by Russia, Prussia and Austria in 1772, 1793, and 1795.

t: Nordic kingdoms establish archdioceses
c: The realms of Denmark, Norway and Sweden established their own archdioceses, responsible directly to the pope, in 1104, 1154 and 1164, respectively.

t: Harald Klak forced to flee Denmark by Horik I
c: In 826, the King of Jutland Harald Klak was forced to flee from Denmark by Horik I, Denmark's other king.

t: Ansgar establishes Christian community in Birka
c: Ansgar traveled to Birka in 829 and established a small Christian community there.

t: Archdiocese of Hamburg founded for Scandinavian conversion
c: In 831 the Archdiocese of Hamburg was founded and assigned responsibility for proselytizing Scandinavia.

c: A Danish invasion force was defeated at the battle of Hjörungavágr in 986.

t: Olaf Tryggvason becomes king of Norway
c: In 995 Olaf Tryggvason became King Olaf I of Norway.

t: Norway returns to paganism after Svolder
c: After Olaf's defeat at the Battle of Svolder in 1000 there was a partial return to paganism in Norway under the rule of the Jarls of Lade.

t: Pope Adrian IV visits Norway
c: Nicholas Breakspear, later Pope Adrian IV, visited Norway from 1152 to 1154.

t: Ansgar begins Christianization of Sweden
c: The first known attempts to Christianize Sweden were made by Ansgar in 830, invited by the Swedish king Björn.

t: Great Summer Army joins Great Heathen Army
c: In 871, the Great Heathen Army was reinforced by another Danish force known as the Great Summer Army led by Guthrum.

t: Great Heathen Army splits into two bands
c: In 875, the Great Heathen Army split into two bands, with Guthrum leading one back to Wessex, and Halfdan taking his followers north.

t: Harald Hardrada challenges for English throne

t: Harald Hardrada killed at Stamford Bridge
c: Hardrada was killed, and his Norwegian army was defeated by Harold Godwinson on 25 September 1066 at the Battle of Stamford Bridge.

t: Amlaíb becomes first king of Dublin
c: In 853 Viking leader Amlaíb (Olaf) became the first king of Dublin.

t: Máel Sechnaill Mór defeats Dublin Vikings at Tara
c: In 980, Máel Sechnaill Mór defeated the Dublin Vikings and forced them into submission at the Battle of Tara.

t: William the Conqueror becomes King of England
c: Rollo's descendant William the Conqueror became King of England after the Battle of Hastings in October 1066.

t: Lothair I recognizes Rorik as Friesland's ruler
c: Around 850, Lothair I acknowledged Rorik as ruler of most of Friesland.

t: Rorik becomes vassal of Charles the Bald
c: In 870 Rorik was received by Charles the Bald in Nijmegen, to whom he became a vassal.

t: Rodulf and his men killed by Oostergo
c: Harald's son Rodulf and his men were killed by the people of Oostergo in 873.

c: Another Viking raid occurred from 859 to 861, apparently by a single group.

t: Erik the Red discovers Greenland
c: In 985, Erik the Red is believed to have discovered Greenland after being exiled from Iceland for murder in 982.

t: Erik the Red returns to Greenland with settlers
c: In 986, Erik the Red returned with 14 surviving ships (25 ships set out on the expedition).

t: Norse settle Greenland's southwest coast
c: Two areas along Greenland's southwest coast were colonised by Norse settlers, including Erik the Red, around 986.

t: Holy Roman Empire establishes Billung March
c: In 936, the Holy Roman Empire set up the Billung and Northern marches in Western Pomerania, divided by the Peene river.
